title: Complete proof of the Dvoretzky-Motzkin cycle lemma in Lean 4

problemStatement.plain: For a ballot sequence with a copies of +1 and b copies of -k satisfying a > k*b, exactly a-k*b cyclic rotations have all partial sums positive.
whyMatters: The cycle lemma is fundamental in combinatorics, underlying Catalan number identities, parking functions, and noncrossing partition theory
Ballot sequences and their rotation counts appear in random walk analysis, queueing theory, and discrete probability
Formalizing the cycle lemma in Lean 4 demonstrates Mathlib combinatorics infrastructure for list and sequence reasoning

proven: goodRotations_card_le: upper bound via prefix sum injection
goodRotations_card_ge: lower bound via levelPos injection from integer levels
level_achieved_ge_min: every integer level in [minPrefixSum, minPrefixSum+sum) is achieved
rightmostAtLevel_good: the rightmost position at each level is a good rotation
open: generalized_ballot_count: exact formula (a-kb)*C(a+b,a) via double-counting (1 sorry remaining)
knownResults.goal: Complete formal proof of |goodRotations l| = a - k*b for {+1,-k}-ballot sequences

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: cycle_lemma proved with 0 sorries in BallotProblemOQ01.lean via goodRotations_card_le + goodRotations_card_ge. ballot_discrete_ivt proved in BallotProblemOQ01OQ01.lean. 1 sorry remains for generalized_ballot_count.
builtItems: BallotProblemOQ01.lean: cycle_lemma proved (|goodRotations l| = a - k*b)
BallotProblemOQ01OQ01.lean: ballot_discrete_ivt proved via Finset.max' argument
insights: Finset.max' technique: define S = {positions with prefix sum <= v}, take max, prove it achieves exactly v
cycle_lemma lower bound: inject integer levels [minPS, minPS+sum) to goodRotations via levelPos
cycle_lemma upper bound: goodRotation_prefixSum_injective shows distinct good rotations have distinct prefix sums
rightmostAtLevel_good: rightmostness handles non-wrapping case; min-prefix-sum bound handles wrapping

approaches.name: Two-bound approach
approaches.description: Prove upper and lower bounds independently, combine via le_antisymm

papers: Dvoretzky, A. and Motzkin, T. (1947). A problem of arrangements. Duke Math. J. 14, 305-313.
